breakfast.name: Banitsa
instructions: Preheat oven to 180C (350F).
Mix crumbled sirene with eggs, yogurt, and baking soda in a bowl.
Brush each filo sheet with melted butter, spread a line of filling along one edge, and roll into a log.
Coil the logs into a round baking dish, spiraling from the center outward.
Brush the top generously with remaining melted butter.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until golden and flaky. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
breakfast.description: Bulgaria's iconic flaky filo pastry filled with tangy white cheese and eggs, coiled into a golden spiral and enjoyed warm for breakfast.

breakfast.name: Mekitsi
ingredients: Powdered sugar or sirene cheese for serving
instructions: Mix flour, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
Add yogurt and egg, stirring until a soft, sticky dough forms.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 170C (340F).
With floured hands, pull off pieces of dough, flatten into discs, and fry until puffed and golden on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve dusted with powdered sugar or topped with crumbled sirene.
breakfast.description: Puffy fried dough rounds made with yogurt, served warm with powdered sugar or salty white cheese, a classic Bulgarian street breakfast.

breakfast.name: Mekitsi (Fried Dough)
ingredients: Powdered sugar or sirene cheese to serve
instructions: Mix yogurt, egg, baking soda
Add flour to form soft sticky dough
With wet hands, shape into flat rounds
Fry in oil until puffed and golden on both sides
Serve with powdered sugar or crumbled sirene cheese
breakfast.description: Puffy yogurt-based fried dough — THE Bulgarian breakfast, made with the country's legendary yogurt. Sweet or savory, your choice.

breakfast.name: Banitsa (Spiral Filo Cheese Pie)
ingredients: Filling: 500g sirene (Bulgarian white cheese), 4 eggs, 200ml yogurt
instructions: Mix crumbled sirene with eggs and yogurt
Brush each filo sheet with butter and oil
Spread filling along one edge
Roll into a log, then coil the log into a spiral in a round pan
Continue adding coiled logs to the spiral
Brush top with remaining butter
Bake at 180°C for 30-35 min until deeply golden and flaky
On New Year's Eve, fortunes written on paper are hidden inside — whoever finds one gets a lucky year
breakfast.description: The spiral filo cheese pie that went viral — the coiling technique creates a dramatic spiral when cut. On New Year's Eve, Bulgarians hide fortune papers and a coin inside. The crunch of the filo and the tang of the sirene cheese make it addictive.

lunch.name: Shopska Salata
instructions: Combine tomatoes, cucumbers, roasted peppers, and onion in a large bowl.
Drizzle with sunflower oil and red wine vinegar. Season with salt and toss gently.
Transfer to a serving plate and top generously with grated sirene cheese.
Garnish with chopped parsley and serve immediately.
lunch.description: The quintessential Bulgarian salad with ripe tomatoes, cucumbers, and roasted peppers topped with a snowy blanket of grated white cheese.

lunch.name: Bob Chorba
ingredients: 2 cups dried white beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Drain soaked beans, cover with fresh water, and boil for 10 minutes. Drain again.
In a large pot, heat oil and saute onion and carrots until soft.
Add tomato paste, paprika, and grated tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add beans and 6 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Cook for 45-50 minutes until beans are tender. Season with salt, pepper, and dried spearmint.
Serve hot with crusty bread.
lunch.description: A hearty Bulgarian white bean soup seasoned with paprika and spearmint, a warming staple of the national cuisine.

lunch.name: Kavarma (Slow-Cooked Meat and Vegetable Stew)
instructions: Brown meat in oil
Sauté onions, peppers, mushrooms
Add tomatoes, paprika, cumin
Transfer to clay pot, add a little water
Bake covered at 180°C for 45-60 min
Crack egg on top, return to oven 5 min until egg sets
Serve in the clay pot
lunch.description: Slow-baked meat stew topped with a cracked egg — served bubbling in traditional Bulgarian clay pots (gyuveche).

dinner.name: Kavarma
instructions: Heat oil in an oven-safe pot and brown pork cubes on all sides.
Add onions and bell peppers, cooking until softened.
Stir in garlic, paprika, and pepper. Add tomatoes and white wine.
Cover and bake at 180C (350F) for 45 minutes until pork is tender.
Make 4 wells in the stew and crack an egg into each. Return to oven for 8 minutes until eggs are set.
Garnish with parsley and serve in the pot.
dinner.description: A traditional Bulgarian clay-pot stew of slow-cooked pork with peppers and tomatoes, finished with baked eggs on top.

dinner.name: Sarmi
instructions: Rinse vine leaves in cold water and pat dry.
Mix ground meats with rice, diced onions, paprika, savory, salt, and pepper.
Place a spoonful of filling on each vine leaf and roll tightly, tucking in the sides.
Arrange rolls seam-side down in a large pot, layering tightly.
Pour tomato juice and 1 cup water over the rolls. Drizzle with oil.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 90 minutes until rice is cooked through.
Serve warm with a dollop of plain yogurt.
dinner.description: Bulgarian stuffed vine leaves filled with seasoned pork, beef, and rice, slowly simmered in tomato juice and served with cool yogurt.

dinner.name: Sarmi (Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: Filling: 400g minced pork and beef, 1 cup rice, 1 onion, paprika, cumin, salt
instructions: Separate sauerkraut leaves carefully
Mix filling: raw mince with rice, diced onion, paprika, cumin, salt
Place filling on each leaf, roll tightly, tuck ends
Layer rolls in pot with smoked ribs between layers
Cover with tomato sauce diluted with water
Simmer on low 90 min or bake covered at 175°C for 2 hours
The sauerkraut gives a tangy depth you can't get from fresh cabbage
dinner.description: Stuffed sauerkraut rolls with smoked meat — the winter celebration dish. Every Bulgarian grandmother guards her recipe.

snacks.name: Printsesa
instructions: Place a slice of kashkaval cheese between two slices of bread and press edges to seal.
Dip the sandwich in flour, then in beaten egg, coating all sides.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown on both sides, about 2 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels, cut in half, and serve warm.
snacks.description: A beloved Bulgarian fried cheese sandwich coated in egg batter, crispy on the outside with melted kashkaval cheese inside.

snacks.name: Lyutenitsa (Pepper and Tomato Relish)
instructions: Roast peppers and eggplants until charred, peel
Peel and chop tomatoes
Blend everything coarsely — keep some texture
Simmer in large pot 45-60 min, stirring often
Add garlic, sugar, vinegar, salt to taste
Cook until thick
Jar hot for preserving, or refrigerate
snacks.description: Roasted pepper and tomato relish — every family makes kilos in September. Spread on bread with sirene cheese for the perfect snack.

desserts.name: Garash Torta
instructions: Beat egg whites with salt to stiff peaks, gradually adding sugar.
Fold ground walnuts gently into the meringue.
Divide into 4 portions and bake each as a thin disc at 170C (340F) for 12 minutes.
Melt chocolate with cream and rum to make a ganache. Let cool slightly.
Layer the walnut meringue discs with ganache between each layer.
Coat the entire cake with remaining ganache and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.
desserts.description: An elegant Bulgarian chocolate-walnut torte with layers of crunchy walnut meringue and rich dark chocolate ganache, a Sofia classic since the 1800s.

desserts.name: Garash Cake
instructions: Whip egg whites with half the sugar to stiff peaks
Fold in ground walnuts gently
Divide into 3-4 layers, bake each at 180°C for 10-12 min
Make chocolate cream: melt chocolate, mix with yolks and remaining sugar
Layer: walnut meringue, chocolate cream, repeat
Pour chocolate glaze over the top
Refrigerate overnight
desserts.description: Bulgaria's most famous cake — walnut meringue layers with chocolate cream, invented at the Garash café in Sofia in 1885.

drinks.name: Ayran
instructions: Combine yogurt, cold water, and salt in a pitcher.
Whisk vigorously or blend until frothy and smooth.
Serve cold in tall glasses, optionally with ice.
drinks.description: A refreshing cold yogurt drink whisked until frothy, the traditional Bulgarian accompaniment to grilled meats and heavy meals.

drinks.name: Rakia
ingredients: Shopska salata or roasted peppers for accompaniment
instructions: Pour rakia into small traditional glasses at room temperature.
Serve alongside a small plate of shopska salata or roasted peppers with sirene.
Sip slowly, alternating with bites of the salad.
drinks.description: Bulgaria's national spirit, a potent fruit brandy typically distilled from grapes or plums, always enjoyed slowly with meze appetizers.

drinks.name: Ayran
instructions: Whisk yogurt until smooth
Add cold water gradually, whisking
Season with salt
Serve very cold
drinks.description: Cold salted yogurt drink — made with Bulgaria's famous yogurt (Lactobacillus bulgaricus). The essential summer drink.
